SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
Patient is a 55-year-old male with new-onset low back pain. Low back pain began on 06/07/2026. He denies trauma, cancer, fever, weight loss, bladder or bowel symptoms, saddle anesthesia, and progressive neurologic deficit. Neurologic examination shows normal lower-extremity strength, reflexes, and sensation. He started NSAIDs today (06/08/2026). Physical therapy is scheduled to begin on 06/12/2026. Assessment: Acute lumbar musculoligamentous strain. Plan: Continue NSAIDs, initiate physical therapy as planned, and re-evaluate in two weeks.

SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
Patient reports completion of a prescribed NSAID course and a 12-session physical therapy program. NSAIDs were started on 06/08/2026 and continued through 07/24/2026 with partial response. Physical therapy was initiated on 06/12/2026, completed 12 sessions by 07/24/2026, and showed no improvement. He denies trauma, cancer, fever, weight loss, bladder or bowel symptoms, saddle anesthesia, and progressive neurologic deficit. Neurologic exam remains normal with symmetric strength and reflexes. Assessment: Chronic low back pain unresponsive to conservative measures. Plan: Obtain lumbar MRI to localize the level before a planned L4-L5 epidural steroid injection; continue activity modification and consider epidural steroid injection after imaging.

Patient returns with persistent low back pain. Lumbar MRI ordered today, 08/06/2026, to localize the symptomatic level prior to a planned L4-L5 epidural steroid injection.
